# PR #475 final whole-PR adversarial audit

**Verdict: SIGN-OFF.** I found no remaining introduced defect that meets the review policy's admission criteria. The original four FIX-IN-PR findings are resolved. No new FIX-IN-PR or DEFER-ISSUE item is admitted by this audit.

Reviewer: fresh independent GPT-6 Astra, requested max effort, under the explicit final-auditor dispatch. This is formal scan **2 of 3 total for PR #475**, including the original Sol review; the count does not reset across revisions. No additional reviewer was dispatched. Parent/root retains disposition, publication and merge authority. Issue #237 owner acceptance and closure remain open.

Audit completed: 2026-11-15 UTC. PR: https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/pull/475.

## Exact identity and admission

| Item | Verified identity |
| --- | --- |
| Head | `30b24ce35d9bcc247579acf54d4efb8153ca0348` |
| Head tree | `6cdf7c4369ae3494bafddaa6f9f83cf9335f2029` |
| Actual main / comparison base | `8fadcb0d44ac2caf80ff6279fe4648ce9398afd9` |
| Branch | `codex/gg-20261114-save-publish` |
| Actual CI merge | `a283b790836207b23e3126d6f794f78433334d3b` |
| CI merge parents, in order | `8fadcb0d44ac2caf80ff6279fe4648ce9398afd9`, `30b24ce35d9bcc247579acf54d4efb8153ca0348` |
| CI merge tree | `6cdf7c4369ae3494bafddaa6f9f83cf9335f2029`, identical to the head tree |
| Native-tested ancestor | `bf9f287652a23177b87488df110dfd6147acaad0` |
| Native-tested tree | `51f8676e5ed738377456f9c70a67d577248df202` |

I independently checked the clean local checkout, branch, Git objects, remote main/head/PR-merge refs, live PR metadata and actual GitHub merge commit object. The final recheck still matched; no identity drift was observed. Parent #474 has actually merged. This audit covers the entire effective child change against actual main, including the final integration context. It is not a renewed audit or sign-off of the parent PR's historical findings.

The full 855-path changed inventory exactly matches `source-and-evidence-readback.json`: every file's byte count, SHA-256 and current Git blob match, with no missing or extra path. The 19 non-QA paths consist of seven production TypeScript/TSX files, five test files, one test fixture, five documentation files and `.prettierignore`. The remaining 836 paths are evidence/archive material or its QA attributes.

I independently reproduced the recorded diff digests using read-only Git output:

| Artifact | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Effective non-QA diff | 192154 | `809df3c147c5eb4a953096de7769e6fa19b4d5a0f54682bbfd47a4897bdf4c70` |
| Full binary diff | 28831727 | `9e0b92c2ce52a965921d268010c4d3f9420d39a37b9124d751f95184e7132810` |
| Dispatch brief | as retained | `1ed2cec282cc2478e0ff8e03a13e1e769203243757f049520492ebb9832ebe6e` |

The diff from the native-tested `bf9f2876` to this head is empty outside `docs/qa` and `docs/delivery`. Inspection of the intervening changes confirms evidence/delivery publication and the authored README final-newline correction with corresponding manifest/checksum updates; no product, test, dependency or build input changed.

## Review scope and method

I read AGENTS.md, `docs/README.md`, the relevant implementation-plan context, `docs/15-issue-workflow.md`, the four-intent delivery register, `REVIEW-COMMON.md`, the #237 architecture/design decisions, the pipeline skill and review policy, and the full final brief, identity and gate records. The accepted contract remains frontend save/publication reconciliation, preserving draft ancestry, current editor work and immutable releases, with truthful delayed/unknown outcome feedback.

I reviewed all 19 non-QA changes and the full affected production modules: `usePublish.ts`, `useAutosave.ts`, `store.ts`, `EditorPage.tsx`, `queries.ts`, `ConflictNotice.tsx` and `WebhookReceiver.tsx`. I read all five changed test files and `fake-api.ts`. Supporting caller review included editor loading/reconciliation, conflict resolution, toolbar and route lifetime, device-draft persistence, voice staging, the API client, loop GET/conditional-save/publish handlers, and the installed TanStack Query cancellation/refetch implementation. I traced ordinary save, unmount save, reload/restore, queued publish, retry readback, response loss, concurrent writer, stale list/detail, validation and later-version schedules.

For the QA archive I read the packet wrappers, original implementation/correction/review reports and root dispositions, integration/source lineage, current CI records and logs, final native report, binding/admission/gateway/matrix code and all three retained final native behavior drivers. I inspected the final raw outcome records and three final screenshots (held-input divergent recovery, older mismatched release with v2 current, and dependent validation after reopening). The 855-file integrity check authenticates archived bytes; it does not imply every historical log line, copied source backup or screenshot was individually semantically reviewed.

This audit itself executed **only read-only inspection and verification**: filesystem reads, Git comparisons/identity queries with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, GitHub reads, and independently written in-memory hashing/parsing checks. It did not execute the retained harnesses or product code, run tests/builds/coverage/browser sessions, access a provider, use the owner service/store, or mutate source/index/remote Git state. The only output written is this external report.

## Whole-change assessment

| Requirement / risk | Assessment and source basis |
| --- | --- |
| Exact acknowledged content | `usePublish.ts:86-92` selects the accepted save response when its revision matches, otherwise canonicalizes a clean loaded/staged copy. `useAutosave.ts:267-287` installs the returned definition/token only for the current load's fully saved revision. Full canonical definition comparison, rather than row ID/version/revision/token alone, determines what a release holds. |
| Dispatch and load ownership | `usePublish.ts:142-185` fences loop/generation and refusals after flush, when the queue reaches the attempt, and after awaited precheck immediately before POST. The hook suppresses old-load feedback (`249-287`). The route remounts by loop ID, and store load/reset clears acknowledgment state. Later authored work is not replaced by a callback. |
| Save ordering and token ancestry | The existing per-loop queue now also owns publish. The autosave hook's per-load chain (`useAutosave.ts:146-156`, `267-279`, `331-358`) advances only from that load's accepted saves; a leaving generation cannot borrow an unrelated reopened load's token. Accepted saves still refresh caches after unmount. Device persistence keeps newer work and request-base ancestry independently of query refresh. |
| Unknown outcome and retry | Uncertainty is retained separately from mutation feedback and scoped to its originating editor load. Local refusals leave it intact. A failing actual retry GET grants no POST; a successful divergent readback records conflict before a later held-input refusal can erase the evidence. A healthy pending acknowledged draft permits one fresh POST after the GET. Known API refusals remain failures. |
| Conflict and device preservation | Divergence enters the established recovery flow only for the same generation still on the acknowledged token (`usePublish.ts:214-227`). Clean revisions are made dirty so the intended graph remains an unsynced device copy. No automatic overwrite or token adoption grants authority over another writer's draft. |
| Publication messages | `publishNotice` (`usePublish.ts:312-415`) names the immutable returned/read-back version, distinguishes a previous unknown request from the current unsent attempt, and limits content claims to that named version. Held field input is described separately. A newer current version is announced without relabeling the old response. Plain confirmations clear on the next edit; other outcomes remain dismissible. |
| Fresh list/detail and async errors | `refreshLoopAfterWrite` (`queries.ts:291-312`) cancels exact pre-write reads before invalidating them, including cold reads with no prior data. It never patches query data from a mutation response, so an old acknowledgment cannot roll back a newer read. The device cache update starts before those reads. TanStack's normal error state retains failed refetches; this helper's promise does not become an unhandled read rejection. |
| Dependent validation | Publication cancels other loops' in-flight validation before marking it stale with no forced refetch. The publishing loop's validation keys are excluded. Normal reopening/refocus/new draft can recheck; a canceled cold check remains Checking until next use, as documented. The native warm/cold records establish the intended subsequent refresh. |
| UI and navigation | The refusal state overrides stale Ready to publish feedback. The existing conflict controls and notice primitives remain in use. The immutable-release notice has no ambiguous loop-level run link; the toolbar's existing New run path remains. Version-pinned execution itself is unchanged and has native evidence. |
| Scope, safety and maintainability | The hook isolates publication state and copy from the editor component; refresh is a bounded shared helper. No new backend API, conditional publish contract, migration, stored/export/device format, provider behavior, dependency or architectural layer is introduced. Imports remain through package boundaries. The only new formatting exclusion is raw QA TSX archives, preserving historical bytes without weakening product formatting or coverage. |
| Documentation | CHANGELOG, numbered frontend documentation and guides reflect current feedback, refusal/readback behavior, cache refresh and run-link semantics. Delivery checkpoints identify historical results and retain failures instead of treating them as current gates. Owner acceptance remains separate. |

The first publish still freezes the draft present at server admission, so another writer can win between local acknowledgment and the POST. This is the accepted existing API boundary. The patch reports that mismatch and preserves the editor copy; a new conditional-publish API is outside the contract. Likewise, same-mounted restored work may wait behind an already-running publication in the authorized per-loop queue. The retained native observation did not establish an independently acknowledged newer draft being blocked, and I found no source-backed new defect in that schedule. These are **NO-CHANGE** assessments, not deferred findings.

## Original findings and correction effectiveness

The original Sol report and root's published disposition comment `6882651485` are retained unchanged. Each was FIX-IN-PR; none was deferred.

| Original root cause | Current resolution and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| F1: known divergent retry still publishes another draft | `usePublish.ts:166-181` selects a changed outcome before any POST, and `214-227` applies conflict preservation. Final native divergent, held-input and initial-readback cases each observed only the original POST; the healthy control observed exactly one additional POST after the verified GET. Exact server/device definitions, old release and tokens are asserted. |
| F2: failed precheck attributes old uncertainty to the newer attempt's draft | `usePublish.ts:337-346` explicitly says the current Publish sent no request and the earlier request remains unknown. The A1/A3 native case asserts the entire factual clause, distinguishable persisted A3 content/token and no second POST. |
| F3: old release incorrectly calls newer published work unpublished | `usePublish.ts:330-335`, `382-412` describes the named version's content and separate held input. The final matched, mismatched and held cases independently publish exact A2 as v2 before releasing v1, then assert the wording, immutable v1/v2 records and absence of a release-specific navigation claim. |
| F4: late dependent validation becomes falsely fresh after publication | `queries.ts:301-311` cancels dependents using normal revert semantics before stale invalidation. Both final warm/cold records show zero immediate/own/unrelated forced rechecks and exactly one fresh validation on ordinary reopening, with B's exact definition/token unchanged and the old dependency error gone. |

The correction packet retains the old-source negative control: 20 intended failures with 32 controls passing out of 52 focused tests. The corrected 52 and 284 related tests passed. The final test sources assert observable requests, exact persisted definitions, held input, stale cache arrival and displayed claims, rather than merely echoing the implementation. Historical native negative schedules also reproduced the designated failures; the early fixture/readback timing corrections remain visible. These are stronger evidence than a green corrected test run alone.

No new finding is being hidden in a NO-CHANGE, DUPLICATE-STALE or deferred bucket. Previously corrected root causes and inherited parent work are not re-raised without contradictory current evidence.

## Current gates and evidence quality

I independently read live job results for CI `43657427543` and routing `43657427557`. All five current-head jobs completed successfully on their first attempts. Actual checkout logs name merge `a283b790836207b23e3126d6f794f78433334d3b`; the Git object independently proves its base/head parents and identical head tree. Retained decoded-log lengths/hashes match the gate record.

| Gate | Current recorded result |
| --- | --- |
| Gates, job `132639035204` | Passed; 22 coverage tasks; web 2598 tests / 210 files; domain 459 / 29; API 1917 passed with 20 skipped; infrastructure 1149 passed with 8 skipped. Type/lint/layer/dependency/license/generated-doc/format checks passed. |
| Browser, job `132639035102` | 479 passed, one expected live-provider skip, zero retries. |
| Windows launcher, job `132639035139` | 14/14 passed. |
| Template image, job `132639034929` | Passed. |
| Routing, job `132638967239` | Passed. |

The configured high-severity dependency-audit threshold passed with **8 low and 13 moderate advisories**, not zero advisories. Earlier bf9/1867 format failures and canceled Browser runs remain historical; the old-parent synthetic merge is not counted as actual-main verification.

The final actual-main native report has SHA-256 `02eaba194ad9731d248d7826f2243e67284a402ab408b77473b91dc3080cfd6d`. It records all **19 outcomes across 14 isolated fixtures on their first executions**, with zero driver/oracle corrections, failures or uncaught page errors. I read the complete drivers and checked the raw outcome totals. Their pre-admission barriers abort/hold before a genuine upstream request; post-commit barriers retain actual gateway responses. Independent HTTP reads and IndexedDB observations establish exact definitions/tokens, immutable records, absence of forbidden requests and preserved device work. The publication controls include a real provider-free run pinned to an older immutable version after the current version advances.

I independently rehashed **1227 current distribution files across 13 trees**, **49 bound source paths**, **17 embedded source-map modules**, and **102 final-native raw packet files**. The file sets and all expected bytes/hashes match. Before/after native binding files are byte-identical, SHA-256 `7c1803d9254d214522548b4a874a361e5882b77afa709f2acff759f9b24f58b7`. The served entry is `/app/assets/index-DBQ4wl7Y.js`, SHA-256 `34bf7a1c90e6b2ba940fb4ea966da091a39a0d37efd559709eb02315fef159e4`; the compiled API main is `e011151e143f07f29181c03f616b6d8e5b7c04e1f136f001b508e9a480c8cc98`. This authenticates the supplied native evidence's source/build lineage through the metadata-only final head movement.

The final build record reports 12 forced tasks with zero cache hits. Unchanged TypeScript outputs may still be incremental; this is not a claim that every backend file was freshly re-emitted. Gateway records use disposable file SQLite and ephemeral loopback, explicitly excluding owner ports 4747/4748 and providers. All 14 owned fixture browser/gateway pairs have retained cleanup evidence. This auditor did not rerun those operations or independently inspect the owner's environment.

## Disposition and limits

**SIGN-OFF applies to head `30b24ce35d9bcc247579acf54d4efb8153ca0348`, tree `6cdf7c4369ae3494bafddaa6f9f83cf9335f2029`, against actual main `8fadcb0d44ac2caf80ff6279fe4648ce9398afd9`.** No additional implementation or review pass is requested by this verdict. One of the three total scan slots remains unused.

The source review is static; runtime conclusions combine the independently inspected native evidence and exact-target CI with current source/build identity checks. Component fake-API coverage, CI browser composition, and compiled-gateway/file-SQLite native evidence are separate tiers. The bounded scenarios do not establish every possible interleaving, physical touch interaction, screen-reader speech, live provider behavior or subjective product acceptance. Those limits do not conceal an identified in-scope blocker.

Root may proceed with its authorized final disposition/publication/merge steps after its own live identity check. Preserve the original findings, failures and this report. Keep `Part of #237`; the owner still needs to judge the clarity and trustworthiness of the actual merged experience before acceptance or issue closure.
